name: Mateo Alston
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I raced a full season with a rival's borrowed rudder.” On Sunday, near Juniper Street, Mateo knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I know where my old racing rival patched the sail. I want the patch to hang beside my silver medal.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a pale blue work shirt and a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. Mateo has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with a neat white crop. Mateo gives a little nod before asking a hard question during a conversation.
personality: Mateo gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Mateo privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To display the rival's repair beside the silver medal.
family: Daryl Trent is Mateo’s cousin. Mateo brings a spare shopping bag. Daryl chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The widow's dividend*, Daryl says, “My pension owns a sliver of this firm. I want the tenants to know we're tied together.”
connections: Lily Wilcox. The tea stain and the racing patch tell two stories from the very same piece of sail.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Mateo clears the dishes, lets the angriest speaker cool off, and resumes the conversation with a smaller audience.
